F1.method: Tenancy types from the reference's designed fact states only (claim_type). Family means: a family's value is the mean over its claim-runs of the type; the type's value is the mean over the families that have such claims (as the paper's subset rows). Contrasts: CasePath minus the comparator over those families, 95% paired cluster-bootstrap interval (10,000 resamples, spec seed), exact two-sided sign-flip p; descriptive. Theft: S = the 72 changed-fact pairs (nine changed-fact clusters, the registered measure), O = the 48 unresolved-fact pairs (six clusters: the conditions that have an unresolved sentence; smallest attainable p 0.031).

F2.method: E(q) = (1 - q) x mean on type S + q x mean on type O, with claim-run means (at the test's own share this reproduces the registered per-claim value; checked) and, beside it, family means. Crossover: the q in [0, 1] where two lines meet (None: parallel or outside 0-1). Band: 10,000 family-bootstrap resamples (24 families with replacement; pooled claim-run means on S and O per resample; a resample without either type is drawn again), percentile 2.5-97.5 per q, for CasePath and the frontier single prompt.

first_draft_h3_ni.definition: first draft (STUDY3_DESIGN.md at 71eaa9eb): CasePath's strict unsafe errors per claim not higher than Rules in context, frontier, by 0.10 or more; paired cluster bootstrap over the 24 families, p = share of resamples reaching the margin

h4_self_consistency.test: exact two-sided sign-flip over the nine changed-fact clusters

F3.method: p values: H1-H3 the registered exact sign-flip p; H4 the largest of its three registered p (all three must hold, so the family passes at alpha only if the largest does); H5 either the registered bootstrap non-inferiority p or the exact one-sided sign-flip non-inferiority p over the nine changed facts (study3_review R5). A 'fewer' hypothesis is confirmed only when the difference favours CasePath. Holm: study2.holm over the five p values; confirmed when the adjusted p < 0.05. Orders: frozen (ANALYSIS_PLAN_STUDY3.md); final draft before the reorder (commit 984d2991); first draft (71eaa9eb), whose tenancy hypothesis was a non-inferiority test against the frontier model (margin 0.10), computed here from the stored plans with study3.run_contrast.

F4.method: (i) CasePath, checklist only (cost-efficient model, three runs): for each stored case-run its three readings are taken from the response cache (a response answering more than half the workflow's facts opens a reading, a smaller one is its requote), each answer admitted as the product does (value, and a quotation found word for word by the product's own Evidence.locate at the tested commit), and the first k readings combined as team.read_facts / team.confirm_facts combine them: a value counts only when all k give it. Routing facts and document findings are kept as stored; presumptions follow the product's rule (workflows.presumed, open rule 'any'); the checklist is the product evaluator's (exact deferral). The check row shows how often k = 3 reproduces the stored checklist. Cost per case-run = the ledger cost of the case-run's calls minus the readings after the k-th (with their requotes). (ii) Self-consistency: the 15 stored samples per case (Rules in context, cost-efficient model) in consecutive disjoint groups of m; floor(15 / m) votes per case, each scored as a run (votes per case: m = 1: 15, 3: 5, 5: 3, 7: 2, 9-15: 1); study3.majority (requested when more than half the samples request it; a tie is not requested); m = 5 reproduces the registered votes (checked). Cost = m x the registered cost per sample. (iii) Budget-matched: the smallest m whose cost is at least the product's; paired contrast with the registered clusters (24 families; nine changed facts), a design's cluster value being the mean over its runs or votes; descriptive.

results.name: perturbed copy of the registered reference (10% of documents moved, seeded; check)
clean room: registered reference as given to the comparison
reading A1: a denied defining event does not stop the process
reading A2: an open defining event is presumed to have occurred
reading A3: optional documents are requested
reading A4: a family-home condition excludes arrears

F5.usage: python3 analysis/study3_feedback.py --alt-reference A.json B.json: each file maps claim id -> document id -> state (required_now, held, not_needed, supplied_sufficient, supplied_insufficient), or claim id -> {document_states: ...} as the stored references; every claim and every document of the registered reference must be present. Subsets, families and everything else stay the registered reference's; every design's stored plans are rescored with study2.ten_row, and the registered tenancy contrasts (H2, H3, S2a-S2f, S3a, S3b) are recomputed with study3's own contrast. The registered reference itself reproduces every stored number (checked).

amendments.A1: a denied defining event does not stop the process: where the defining-event fact (termination_received, claim_received) is admitted false, the evaluator is given it as true (as if the event had occurred). A fact left open keeps the gate open (held), as in the A1 reference. Not done at workflow level: a gate that passes on true or false would also stop holding an open event, which the A1 reference does not do.
amendments.A2: an open defining event is presumed to have occurred: the routed presumption (true) also applies when the readings raise the event and leave it open; it still does not apply when a reading found a value other than true, or when the readings conflict (workflows.reading_gave_value; status 'conflicting').
amendments.A3: optional documents are requested like mandatory ones: the 'optional' mark is removed from the workflow's optional documents (defect: caretaker_correspondence; termination and rent: landlord_correspondence); the evaluator then requests them where their step is reached and holds them where it depends on an open fact.
amendments.A4: the family-home branch needs family_home and not arrears: in lease_termination_dispute the edge lt_type__gate_family_home -> lt_family becomes {all: [family_home is true, arrears is false]} and the edge -> lt_abuse becomes {any: [family_home is false, arrears is true]}; spouse_notice_copy's own condition (family_home) is left as it is, since its step is now reached only through the amended edge.

F5b.method: Each product design's stored tenancy case-runs are replayed from their stored readings (k = 3, the first three readings in the response cache, admitted with the product's own quotation check), with routing and document findings as stored, by the product's evaluator at the tested commit, with the workflow (A3, A4) or the facts given to the evaluator (A1, A2) amended to the reading; needs added by an agent are kept as stored (none entered a checklist). Unamended, the replay reproduces the stored scored checklist in 285 of 286 evaluated case-runs of the full product and of checklist only, and in 95 of 96 of the frontier one-run row; the two failed case-runs keep their stored (empty) plans. Routing is kept as stored: every denied-event claim-run was routed to its dispute's workflow in the stored runs, so no claim changes routing under a reading. Each replay is scored against the reference written under the same reading (cleanroom/evaluator_b/reference_alt_*.json); subset membership is the registered reference's. The baselines are not re-run: their stored plans are scored against the same alternative reference. Their prompts carried the registered rule text, so wherever they ignored the registered stop (and requested documents on a denied event) the alternative reference favours them. The reverse also holds: where a reading changes what the registered rule text told every design (A2, A3, A4), a baseline that followed the registered text is scored against a reading it was never given, while the matched CasePath was given it; those contrasts therefore compare a design told the reading with designs that were not, and A3 in particular widens the gap for that reason (every design was told not to request optional documents). Contrasts: CasePath (matched workflow, full product) minus each baseline over the 24 families, 95% cluster bootstrap with the registered resamples, exact sign-flip p; post hoc and descriptive.
